Prevention: Avoid close planting and continuous water stagnation at early stages.
Conserve natural enemies such as dragonflies (Oosi thattan), spiders (Silanthi), parasitic wasps (Kulavi) by reducing the amount of insecticides usage.
Follow crop rotation (e.g. legumes/vegetables for two to three years).
Monitoring: Look for egg masses on the leaf tips and on the underside of the leaves.
Egg masses are brownish yellow coloured and present on the upper surface of leaves.
Observe during the vegetative stage, larvae bore at the base of the plants, killing growing points which result in dead heart (central tiller dries up and is easily pulled from the base).
Monitor weekly from seedling to harvest for the presence of the insect and damage symptoms.
During the reproductive stage, larvae bore through the upper nodes and feed towards the base, resulting in whiteheads (emerging panicles are whitish and empty).
Larvae leave tiny holes on the stems and tillers, and inside the damaged stems.
Direct Control: Install pheromone traps at 5 per acre from planting and observe during 7-9pm.
Set up light traps at 1 per acre and observe from 7-9 pm to control adult moths in the field.
Trichogramma japonicum 3 at 2 cc/acre at 30 and 37
Nimbicidine at 300 ml per acre at 15 days interval twice a month.
Bacillus thuringiensis var kurstaki 1 ml/lit of water and
Neem seed kernel extract in combination of 2.5 kg/l of water to reduce the oviposition by stem borer.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
